extracted.intended_audience: general readers, film viewers, critics, and researchers interested in the film Four Lions
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia encyclopedia entry summarizing the 2010 British black comedy film Four Lions: its plot, production, release, critical reception, box office, and accolades. The page presents both descriptive facts and critics' evaluative language about the film's humour, themes, and performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screenplay
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical praise and evaluation of the screenplay — the article states the film 'received positive reviews from critics, with praise for the screenplay, direction, themes, humour, and cast performances.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers credited: Chris Morris, Sam Bain, Jesse Armstrong; Armstrong and Bain provided the first script which Morris subsequently rewrote and edited. Critics' assessments of the screenplay factor heavily into overall reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction (directorial debut)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of Chris Morris's direction, including that this was his directorial debut and that direction was among elements critics praised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morris spent years researching the project and directing choices are discussed alongside screenplay and themes; the article notes Morris won the BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Debut.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humour and tone (pitch-black satire)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the film's comedic tone — Rotten Tomatoes consensus: 'Its premise suggests brazenly tasteless humor, but Four Lions is actually a smart, pitch-black comedy that carries the unmistakable ring of truth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly frames the film as a 'black comedy' and 'farce' that satirises terrorism; reviewers debate whether its humour is tasteful or offensively provocative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cast performances and comic timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical attention to acting and timing — the article highlights praise for cast performances, particularly Riz Ahmed and Kayvan Novak, and notes 'the actors displaying sharp comic timing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cast performance is discussed as central to the film's success; specific awards/nominations for performances (e.g., Kayvan Novak winning Best Comedy Performance) are cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity / realism of portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgements about how 'real' or authentic the film's evocation of characters and community life feels — The Daily Telegraph wrote the film's 'evocations of the claustrophobic mundanity of the Muslims' lives... all feel painfully, brilliantly real.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morris' reported research (interviews with terrorism and religion experts, law enforcement, British Muslims) and pre-release screening with Moazzam Begg are presented as supporting the film's realism and sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controversy and offensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the film is controversial or offensive — the director said he 'does not find the film at all controversial' and hopes it is seen as 'not a hate film,' yet there were calls for bans and debate in the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article records both the director's intent ('not a hate film') and public/press responses (calls for bans, screening reactions), indicating controversy is an evaluative dimension for the film.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box office / commercial performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial success measures including opening weekend site average, total grosses, number of screens and expansions — e.g., generated the highest site average (£5,292) on opening weekend, grossed £6 million worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box office figures and distribution (limited release, increase in screens) are used to evaluate the film's market performance and popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival recognition and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Festival and awards-based evaluation — premiered at Sundance (short-listed for World Cinema Narrative prize), BAFTA win for Outstanding British Debut, nominations and other awards mentioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Festival selections, shortlistings, nominations and wins are listed as markers of critical recognition and industry esteem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative critical framing / influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of comparisons to other works and genres in critical evaluation — e.g., reviewers compared Four Lions to This Is Spinal Tap and The Three Stooges and called it 'a brilliant takedown of the imbecility of fanaticism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons to established films/genres and descriptors from major outlets (LA Times, Hollywood Reporter, Variety) are presented as part of critics' appraisal and positioning of the film.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production research and collaborative writing practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Production practices presented as part of the film's formation and implicit quality criteria: Morris 'spent three years researching the project, speaking to terrorism experts, police, the secret service, and imams, as well as ordinary Muslims' and brought in Jesse Armstrong and Sam Bain for their comedy dialogue expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article describes script development (initial script by Armstrong and Bain, subsequent rewrites by Morris), research, funding approaches (crowdfunding email 'Funding Mentalism'), and filming locations — implying thorough research and collaboration are valued in producing sensitive satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterisation and depiction of Muslim lives
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of how the film depicts Muslim characters and community life — critics noted 'their querulous banter, their flimsily pick 'n' mix approach to the Koran' and the film was discussed in terms of challenging stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page records both critical observations about character depiction and reactions from Muslim figures (e.g., Moazzam Begg enjoyed it), indicating depiction legitimacy/sensitivity is a criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent and moral framing (farce vs. hate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the filmmaker's stated intent and moral framing — Morris described the film as a 'farce' and said it was an attempt to 'figure it out' and that it was 'good-hearted' rather than a hate film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The director's stated intent (not attempting to cause controversy, the film being 'good-hearted') is presented alongside critics' and public reactions as a lens for evaluating the film's ethical stance and comedic purpose.
